description: Rule Influence Panel — identifies generation rules that have been loaded many times without measurable positive effect, helping developers prune ineffective rules that waste prompt tokens.

groups.name: Rule Influence Overview
groups.description: Users need to see which generation rules are ineffective, with load counts and prevention rates, to decide which rules should be disabled or improved.

assertions.description: Users can identify the Rule Influence panel and understand its purpose as a tool for evaluating generation rule effectiveness
Each rule row shows how many times the rule has been loaded into generation prompts, indicating how frequently it consumes prompt tokens
Each rule row shows the number of times it was loaded without producing any measurable positive effect, highlighting wasted prompt tokens
Each rule row shows how many times the rule successfully prevented errors or issues, demonstrating its value

groups.name: Rule Effectiveness Ratio
groups.description: Users need a clear effectiveness ratio for each rule to quickly assess which rules contribute value.

assertions.description: Each rule displays an effectiveness percentage derived from its prevention rate vs load count, providing a single metric for rule value assessment
The effectiveness metric is clearly labeled so users understand it represents the ratio of useful rule activations to total loads

groups.name: High No-Effect Warning Badges
groups.description: Rules with high no-effect counts are flagged with an orange warning badge.

assertions.description: Rules that have been loaded many times without effect display an orange warning badge to draw attention to candidates for removal or improvement

groups.name: Loading and Empty States
groups.description: Empty state communicates that all rules appear healthy.

assertions.description: Users see a loading indicator while rule influence data is being fetched, preventing confusion about a blank panel
When no rules have high no-effect counts, users see a positive message indicating all rules are contributing value

groups.name: Rule Data Rendering
groups.description: Each rule row must accurately render the rule ID (first 16 chars, monospace), total loaded count, no-effect count, prevented-error count, and calculated effectiveness ratio.

assertions.description: Rule IDs are shown truncated to 16 characters in monospace font to fit the layout while remaining identifiable
assertions.expected: First 16 characters of rule_id in monospace font

assertions.description: Each rule shows an effectiveness percentage calculated as (prevented_error_count / total_loaded_count * 100), colored green when >50% and orange when <=50%
assertions.expected: Percentage computed as (prevented_error_count / total_loaded_count * 100), green when >50%, orange when <=50%

groups.name: Rule State Transitions
groups.description: The panel transitions between loading, error, empty ('All rules appear effective'), and populated states without visual glitches.

assertions.description: When no ineffective rules exist, the empty state shows a positive message ('All rules appear effective' with ShieldCheck icon) rather than a generic 'no data' message
assertions.precondition: No rules meet the ineffectiveness threshold (this is the healthy state)

states.name: Loading — Fetching Rule Influence Data
states.description: The panel is loading rule influence data from the backend. A loading indicator is displayed to prevent confusion about a blank panel.

transitions.name: No ineffective rules found
transitions.description: Data fetch completes and no rules meet the ineffectiveness threshold, showing the positive empty state

transitions.name: Ineffective rules found
transitions.description: Data fetch completes and one or more rules meet the ineffectiveness threshold, displaying the rule list

transitions.name: Data fetch fails
transitions.description: The API request fails, transitioning to an error state

states.name: All Effective — No Ineffective Rules
states.description: No rules meet the ineffectiveness threshold. A positive message ('All rules appear effective' with ShieldCheck icon) communicates that all rules are contributing value. This is the normal/healthy state.

states.name: Populated — Ineffective Rules Listed
states.description: One or more ineffective rules are displayed in a list. Each row shows the truncated rule ID (monospace), loaded count, no-effect count, prevented count, and effectiveness percentage. Rules with high no-effect counts display an orange warning badge.

states.name: Error — Data Fetch Failed
states.description: The API request to fetch rule influence data has failed. An error message is displayed.

metadata.author: Joshua Spinak
preconditions: Requires multiple workflow generations with rule_influence_log tracking enabled
Rules appear here only when they have >= 3 'no_effect' entries and 0 'prevented_error' entries
The positive empty state ('All rules appear effective') is the normal/healthy state
backendDependencies: GET /graph/ineffective-rules?threshold=3 — returns IneffectiveRule[] with rule_id, no_effect_count, prevented_error_count, total_loaded_count
